answer: Under a lotus anchor scheme, each agent identity is tied to one non-transferable credential backed by a locked stake. Joining requires publishing a cipher commitment that binds the agent's public key to that stake and to proof of prior useful work. The registry rejects a second credential using the same stake or key, so an attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand stakes and repeat the work a thousand times. Honest agents pay once, while Sybil creation scales linearly in cost.
